record.original_question: Give a universal decoding algorithm for quasi-cyclic codes, where a code C is quasi-cyclic of index k if v ∈ C implies σ^k(v) ∈ C for the cyclic shift σ.

evidence.quote: A code C is quasi-cyclic of index k if v ∈ C implies σk(v) ∈ C.
Open Question 10.2. Give a universal decoding algorithm for quasi-cyclic codes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $\sigma:\mathbb{F}_q^n \to \mathbb{F}_q^n$ denote the cyclic shift $\sigma(v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_{n-1}) = (v_{n-1},v_0,\ldots,v_{n-2})$. For a positive integer $k$ dividing $n$, a linear code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ is called quasi-cyclic of index $k$ if $\sigma^k(v) \in C$ for every $v \in C$.

Provide a universal decoding algorithm for the class of quasi-cyclic codes: that is, exhibit an explicit algorithm which, given as input the parameters of an arbitrary quasi-cyclic code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of index $k$ (for example, a generator or parity-check matrix) together with a received word $y \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, returns a codeword $c \in C$ minimizing the Hamming distance $d(y,c)$ (or, more generally, decodes up to half the minimum distance of $C$), with correctness and complexity guarantees that hold uniformly across the family of quasi-cyclic codes.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature indicates that no efficient universal decoding algorithm for general quasi-cyclic codes is known. The Quasi-Cyclic Syndrome Decoding Problem has been shown to be NP-complete (2023), and the BIKE/HQC code-based cryptosystems rely on the presumed hardness of decoding random quasi-cyclic codes. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Decoding Quasi-Cyclic codes is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that the Quasi-Cyclic Syndrome Decoding Problem is NP-complete, supporting the absence of an efficient universal decoder.
status_evidence.claim: No efficient general decoding algorithm for quasi-cyclic codes is known; decoding is NP-complete.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-cyclic Syndrome Decoding problem — Decoding Challenge
status_evidence.snippet: Active decoding challenge for random quasi-cyclic binary linear codes, indicating no efficient universal decoder exists in practice.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-cyclic decoding remains an active research challenge.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-twisted codes: decoding and applications in code-based cryptography
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work continues to study decoding techniques for quasi-cyclic/quasi-twisted codes.
status_evidence.claim: Decoding of quasi-cyclic codes is still an active research topic.
